question.text: The 'privately pooled' nature of AIFs means that:

answer.text: The fund raises money through public issue
The fund pools capital from select investors, not from the general public
The fund is managed by a private company
The fund invests only in private companies

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says "privately pooled" means capital is pooled from select investors and not from the general public at large. AIFs raise corpus only through private placement and are prohibited from inviting the public to subscribe to their units. The Trap: "Private" in "privately pooled" refers to the fundraising method (private placement from select investors), not the ownership of the manager or the type of investee companies. Note: The select-investor / no-general-public / private-placement contrast is the defining feature in the workbook.
